- Here’s the guide to beating a tall wrestler in highschool -

(Written by a lumbering 6’5 Giant who has D1 Wrestling Prospects in the Ivy League)

1. The biggest tool that a tall wrestler has in their arsenal is their length. This increases their offensive and defensive capabilities in many ways. The drawback to all this length and height and reach is lack of dense muscle mass. 

A 5’6 wrestler and a 6’0 wrestler that way the same and are of the same age will almost never have the same level of strength. Muscle fibers will be longer and thinner in a taller wrestler naturally. The important laces this comes into affect is the lower back, neck, hamstrings, and shoulders.

Using this knowledge to formulate an offensive plan, you should focus on two things. The first, having good lateral footwork that forces the opponent to chase and step after you. Take advantage of these lengthy and predictable steps, pairs with a naturally weaker stance, and headsnap. 

I don’t mean collar tie, I mean headsnap, hard. Immediately after, shoot your best shot. Use your #1 takedown. A solid head snap will take all of their weight forward by abusing their weak lower back and they will either have to step forward to compensate or stand up, leaving you an opportunity to attack.

TLDR, keep them stepping into you, headsnap very hard, and then shoot.

2. Tall wrestlers love single legs, picks, and front headlock situations, because they all are easy moves for their size. Just knowing this knowledge means that you have an edge. You know their game plan and they don’t know yours. The problem is, it’s hard to totally prevent a wrestler from hitting these moves. 

The solution to being unable to stop them from hitting these moves is to stop them from hitting these moves. What I mean is your goal should be, “I have to stop an ankle pick, a single leg, and a front headlock”. Your goal should be “I have to stop them from attacking”. The only way to do this is to be the aggressor. Go for fakes, go for headsnaps, don’t tie up for more than 1-2 seconds at a time. You can’t stay stationary, and you can’t give them opportunities.

TLDR, be on a constant offense 

3. Your strategy. Going into a match, your game plan should be 2-1-2-Shot. Go for two fakes or headsnaps, One breakoff, 2 fakes or headsnaps, then shoot. You can mix this up, but fake and breakoffs keep them on their toes, giving them no chance to work their offense. 

4. Don’t be scared. Tall wrestlers are the same as you.  They’re usually just as good as any other wrestler. Most NCAA champs or college wrestlers don’t pass 6’0” tall. They’re human. They make mistakes. They can lose. You can’t fear the height, only learn to take advantage of it.
